questions.question: The speed of a train is 108 km/h. The distance covered by the train in 11 seconds will be:
questions.questionHtml: The speed of a train is 108 km/h. The distance covered by the train in 11 seconds will be:
questions.solution: Speed = 108 × 5/18 m/s = 30 m/s, Distance = 30 × 11 = 330 m

questions.question: A train running at the speed of 63km/h crosses a pole in 24 seconds. What is the length of the train?
questions.questionHtml: A train running at the speed of 63km/h crosses a pole in 24 seconds. What is the length of the train?
questions.solution:
63 km/h = 17.5m/s, Distance travelled =length of the train

Distance = 17.5 × 24 = 420 m

questions.question: P and Q start running in opposite directions on a circular track from the same point. If their speeds are 10 m/s and 8 m/s, respectively, then after what time will they meet if the length of the track is 1620 m?
questions.questionHtml: P and Q start running in opposite directions on a circular track from the same point. If their speeds are 10 m/s and 8 m/s, respectively, then after what time will they meet if the length of the track is 1620 m?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

When two persons run in opposite directions, their relative speed is the sum of their individual speeds.

Relative speed = 10 + 8 = 18 m/s

Time taken to meet = Total track distance ÷ Relative speed

Time = 1620 ÷ 18 = 90 seconds

∴ The correct answer is 90 seconds.

Alternate Method

Given:

Speed of P = 10 m/s

Speed of Q = 8 m/s

Length of the track (Total Distance) = 1620 m

Formula Used:

Relative Speed (Opposite Directions) = S1 + S2

Time = Distance ÷ Relative Speed

Calculations:

⇒ Relative Speed = 10 + 8

⇒ Relative Speed = 18 m/s

⇒ Time taken to meet = 1620 ÷ 18

⇒ Time taken to meet = 90 seconds

∴ The correct answer is 90 seconds.

Additional Information

Relative Speed in Opposite Directions

When two objects move in opposite directions, their relative speed is the sum of their individual speeds (v1 + v2).

Relative Speed in Same Direction

When two objects move in the same direction, their relative speed is the absolute difference of their individual speeds (|v1 − v2|).

Time to Meet at the Starting Point

The time taken for two persons to meet exactly at the starting point is the LCM of the individual times taken by them to complete one full round.

Distinct Meeting Points

If two persons run at speeds 'a' and 'b' (where a and b are co-prime integers), they meet at (a + b) distinct points if moving in opposite directions, and |a − b| distinct points if moving in the same direction.

questions.question: What distance will be covered by a bus moving at 108 km/h in 40 seconds?
questions.questionHtml: What distance will be covered by a bus moving at 108 km/h in 40 seconds?
questions.solution: D = 108 × \(\frac{40}{3600}\) ⇒ D = 1.2 km = 1 km 200 m

questions.question: In a circular race of 1500 m. Anil and Bilal start from the same point and at the same time with speeds of 36 km/h and 54 km/h respectively. When will they meet again for the first time on the track when they are running in the same direction?
questions.questionHtml: In a circular race of 1500 m. Anil and Bilal start from the same point and at the same time with speeds of 36 km/h and 54 km/h respectively. When will they meet again for the first time on the track when they are running in the same direction?
questions.solution:
Given: 

The distance of the circular path race = 1500 m

Anil's speed = 36 km/hr

Bilal's speed = 54 km/hr

Both start from the same point and at the same time and run in the same direction.

Concept used:

When A and B are moving with x km/hr and y km/hr, respectively

In the same direction,

then Relative speed = (x - y) km/hr

In the opposite direction,

then Relative speed = (x + y) km/hr

Formula used:

Conversion of km/hr to m/sec

1 km/hr = (5/18) m/sec

Distance = speed x time

Calculation:

According to the question,

They are moving in the same direction,

Relative speed = (54 - 36) km/hr

⇒ Relative speed = 18 km/hr

⇒ Relative speed = 18 x (5/18) m/sec

⇒ Relative speed = 5 m/sec

As we know that,

Distance = Speed x time

⇒ Time = Distance/speed

⇒ Time = 1500/5 = 300 sec

∴ The answer is 300 sec.

Alternate MethodFormula used:

Time taken to meet for the 1st time = Length of the track/Relative Speed

Time taken = L/u+v, when moving in the opposite direction.

Time taken = L/u-v, when moving in the same direction.

Where, L = Length of the track

u = Speed of A, v = speed of B

1 km/hr = (5/18) m/sec

Calculation:

Time taken to meet for the 1st time = 1500/[(54-36) x (5/18)]

So, time taken for meeting for the 1st time = 1500/5 = 300 sec

∴ The answer is 300 sec.

questions.question: The ratio of the distances Ravina and Suhel had to travel from their respective houses to their workplaces was 4 ∶ 7. If Suhel had to travel 63 km, how much did Ravina have to travel?
questions.questionHtml: The ratio of the distances Ravina and Suhel had to travel from their respective houses to their workplaces was 4 ∶ 7. If Suhel had to travel 63 km, how much did Ravina have to travel?
questions.solution: If Suhel travel 63 km that is 9 × 7, So Ravina travelled 9 ×  4 = 36 km.

questions.question: The ratio between the speeds of two cars is 5 ∶ 7. If the first car runs 200 km in 4 hours, then what is the speed of second car?
questions.questionHtml: The ratio between the speeds of two cars is 5 ∶ 7. If the first car runs 200 km in 4 hours, then what is the speed of second car?
questions.solution:
The speed of the first car = 200 km / 4 hours = 50 km/h.

If speed ratio is 5 ∶ 7, then the speed of second car is 7/5 × speed of first car.

Speed of second car = 7/5 × 50 km/h = 70 km/h.

questions.question: A train of length 180 m takes 40 seconds to cross a tunnel of length 500 m. What is the speed of the train, in km/h?
questions.questionHtml: A train of length 180 m takes 40 seconds to cross a tunnel of length 500 m. What is the speed of the train, in km/h?
questions.solution:
Speed of train (km/h) = (Length of train + Length of tunnel) / Total time taken to cross the tunnel

⇒ Speed of train (m/s) = \(\frac{180 + 500}{40}\)

⇒ Speed of train (m/s) =\(\frac{680}{40}\) ⇒ 17

⇒ Speed of train (km/h) = 17 \( \times \frac{18}{5}\) = 61.2 km/hr

questions.question: A policeman starts chasing a thief who is 500 m ahead of him. The speed of the thief is 18 km/h, and the speed of the policeman is 36 km/h. Find the time taken by the policeman to catch the thief.
questions.questionHtml: A policeman starts chasing a thief who is 500 m ahead of him. The speed of the thief is 18 km/h, and the speed of the policeman is 36 km/h. Find the time taken by the policeman to catch the thief.
questions.solution:
Speed of thief = 18 km/h = 18 × 5 /18 m/s = 5 m/s,

Speed of policeman = 36 km/h = 36 × 5 / 18 m/s = 10 m/s,

Relative speed = 10 m/s - 5 m/s = 5 m/s ⇒ Distance = 500 m,

Time = 500 / 5 = 100 seconds

questions.question: The time taken to travel the same distance by three cars is in the ratio of 12 ∶ 15 ∶ 10. What is the ratio of the speeds of the three cars?
questions.questionHtml: The time taken to travel the same distance by three cars is in the ratio of 12 ∶ 15 ∶ 10. What is the ratio of the speeds of the three cars?
questions.solution:
When traveling the same distance, speed ∝ (1/time)

Speed of the three cars = 12 : 15 : 10

Then, ratio of time of the three cars = (1/12) ∶ (1/15) ∶ (1/10)

Ratio of time = 60/12) ∶ (60/15) ∶ (60/10) = 5 ∶ 4 ∶ 6

questions.question: The distance travelled by a person varies directly with the duration of the journey. If the person travels 378 km in 7 hour, in how many hours will the person cover 918 km?
questions.questionHtml: The distance travelled by a person varies directly with the duration of the journey. If the person travels 378 km in 7 hour, in how many hours will the person cover 918 km?
questions.solution:
Speed of 1st journey = Speed of the second journey

378/7 = 918/T2  ⇒ T2 = (918 × 7)/378 = 17 hours

questions.question: A runner runs a 750-metre race in 54 seconds. Find the runner’s speed (in km/h).
questions.questionHtml: A runner runs a 750-metre race in 54 seconds. Find the runner’s speed (in km/h).
questions.solution: The runner's speed = (750 / 54 ) meter/second = \(750\times 3600\over 54\times 1000\) = 50 km/h.

questions.question: A policeman is chasing a thief at a speed of 82 km/h. The thief is 1300 m away and is running at a speed of 64 km/h. In how much time will the policeman catch the thief if both are riding on bikes?
questions.questionHtml: A policeman is chasing a thief at a speed of 82 km/h. The thief is 1300 m away and is running at a speed of 64 km/h. In how much time will the policeman catch the thief if both are riding on bikes?
questions.solution:
Relative speed = 82 - 64 = 18 km/h = 5 m/s

Time = 1300 m / 5 m/s = 260 sec

questions.question: A thief is noticed by a policeman from a distance of 92 m. The thief starts running and the policeman chases him. The thief and the policeman run at the speed of 90 km/h and 104.4 km/h, respectively. In how much time will the policeman catch the thief?
questions.questionHtml: A thief is noticed by a policeman from a distance of 92 m. The thief starts running and the policeman chases him. The thief and the policeman run at the speed of 90 km/h and 104.4 km/h, respectively. In how much time will the policeman catch the thief?
questions.solution:
Distance = 92 m, Speedthief = 25 m/s, Speedpoliceman = 29 m/s,

⇒ Relative speed = 29 - 25 = 4 m/s 

⇒ Time = 92 / 4 = 23 seconds

questions.question: A thief seeing a policeman from a distance of 300 m starts running at a speed of 10 km/h. The policeman gives chase immediately at a speed of 12 km/h and the thief is caught. What is the distance run by the thief?
questions.questionHtml: A thief seeing a policeman from a distance of 300 m starts running at a speed of 10 km/h. The policeman gives chase immediately at a speed of 12 km/h and the thief is caught. What is the distance run by the thief?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Ratio of Speeds (Policeman : Thief) = 12 : 10 = 6 : 5

Since time is constant, Distance ratio is also 6 : 5

Difference in distance parts = 6 − 5 = 1 unit

Given 1 unit = 300 m = 0.3 km

Distance run by Thief = 5 units = 5 × 0.3 km = 1.5 km

∴ The correct answer is 1.5 km.

Alternate Method

Given:

Initial distance between Policeman and Thief = 300 m = 0.3 km

Speed of Thief (Vt) = 10 km/h

Speed of Policeman (Vp) = 12 km/h

Formula Used:

Relative Speed = Speed of Policeman − Speed of Thief (when moving in the same direction)

Time = Distance ÷ Relative Speed

Distance = Speed × Time

Calculations:

⇒ Relative Speed = 12 − 10 = 2 km/h

⇒ Time taken to catch the thief = 0.3 ÷ 2 = 0.15 hours

⇒ Distance run by the Thief = Speed of Thief × Time

⇒ Distance = 10 × 0.15

⇒ Distance = 1.5 km

∴ The correct answer is 1.5 km.

Additional Information

Relative Speed in Same Direction

When two objects move in the same direction, the relative speed is the difference of their individual speeds: (V1 − V2).

Conversion of Speed Units

To convert km/h to m/s, multiply by 5/18. To convert m/s to km/h, multiply by 18/5.

Constant Time Concept

If two objects start and meet at the same time, the ratio of their distances is equal to the ratio of their speeds: D1/D2 = S1/S2.

questions.question: An inspector is 288 metres behind a thief. The inspector runs 42 metres and the thief runs 30 metres in a minute. In how much time will the inspector catch the thief?
questions.questionHtml: An inspector is 288 metres behind a thief. The inspector runs 42 metres and the thief runs 30 metres in a minute. In how much time will the inspector catch the thief?
questions.solution:
Relative speed = 42 - 30 = 12 meters/minute

Time taken = 288 meters / 12 meters/minute = 24 minutes

questions.question: A girl travels 30 km at a speed of 15 km/h. She travels another 20 km at a speed of 10 km/h. What is her average speed for the entire journey?
questions.questionHtml: A girl travels 30 km at a speed of 15 km/h. She travels another 20 km at a speed of 10 km/h. What is her average speed for the entire journey?
questions.solution: Average speed = \(\frac{30+20}{\frac{30}{15}+\frac{20}{10}}\) = 12.5km/h

questions.question: A thief is noticed by a policeman from a distance of 97 m. The thief starts running and the policeman chases him. The thief and the policeman run at a speed of 21 m/sec and 23 m/sec respectively. What is the time taken by the policeman to catch the thief?
questions.questionHtml: A thief is noticed by a policeman from a distance of 97 m. The thief starts running and the policeman chases him. The thief and the policeman run at a speed of 21 m/sec and 23 m/sec respectively. What is the time taken by the policeman to catch the thief?
questions.solution:
Initial distance = 97m 

Relative Speed = 23 - 21 = 2m/sec

Time is taken to catch the thief = 97/2 = 48.5 sec

questions.question: A train covers the distance between two stations X and Y in 6 hours. If the speed of the train is reduced by 13 km/h, then it travels the same distance in 9 hours. Find the distance between the two stations
questions.questionHtml: A train covers the distance between two stations X and Y in 6 hours. If the speed of the train is reduced by 13 km/h, then it travels the same distance in 9 hours. Find the distance between the two stations
questions.solution:
Let the initial speed be x, 

⇒ x × 6 = (x - 13) × 9 ⇒ 3x = 117 ⇒ x = 39 kmph

Distance = 39 × 6 = 234 km.

questions.question: Anil and Arun started for car race from the same point in the same direction and at the same time on a circular track of length 2575 m with speeds 72 km/h and 90 km/h, respectively. After how much time (in seconds) will they meet again for the first time?
questions.questionHtml: Anil and Arun started for car race from the same point in the same direction and at the same time on a circular track of length 2575 m with speeds 72 km/h and 90 km/h, respectively. After how much time (in seconds) will they meet again for the first time?
questions.solution:
Given: 

The length of the circular track = 2575 m

Anil's speed = 72 km/h

Arun's speed = 90 km/h

Concept used:

When A and B are moving with x km/h and y km/h, respectively in the same direction,

Relative speed = (x - y) km/h

Formula used:

1 km/h = (5/18) m/s

Speed = Distance / Time

Calculation:

Anil and Anuj are running in the same direction,

Relative speed = (90 - 72) km/h = 18 km/h

⇒ Relative speed = 18 x (5/18) m/s = 5 m/s

Time = Distance / Speed

⇒ Time = 2575 / 5 = 515 s

∴ They will meet again for the first time after 515 seconds.

questions.question: A man can cover a certain distance in 2 hours and 10 minutes if he walks at the rate of 12 km/hr. If he covers the same distance on cycle at the rate of 13 km/hr, then find the time taken by him.
questions.questionHtml: A man can cover a certain distance in 2 hours and 10 minutes if he walks at the rate of 12 km/hr. If he covers the same distance on cycle at the rate of 13 km/hr, then find the time taken by him.
questions.solution:
Distance = Speed of walking × Time taken to walk = 12 km/hr × 2.167 hours = 26 km

Time taken to cycle = Distance/Speed of cycling = 26 km/13 km/hr = 2 hours = 120 minutes

questions.question: A car travels from Lucknow to Kanpur at a speed of 65 km/h and comes back at a speed of 60 km/h. If the distance between Lucknow and Kanpur is 80 km, then what is the average speed of the car during the whole journey?
questions.questionHtml: A car travels from Lucknow to Kanpur at a speed of 65 km/h and comes back at a speed of 60 km/h. If the distance between Lucknow and Kanpur is 80 km, then what is the average speed of the car during the whole journey?
questions.solution:
Given:

Distance = 80km

Speed 1 = 65km/h

Speed 2 = 60km/h

Formula used:

Average speed = Total Distance / Total Time taken

Speed = Distance/Time 

Solution:

From Lucknow to Kanpur;

Speed = 65km/h

Distance = 80km

Time = 80/65 = 16/13 hours

From Kanpur to Lucknow;

Speed = 60km/h

Distance = 80km

Time = 80/60 = 4/3 hours

Now,

Total time taken = 16/13 + 4/3  = 100/39 hours

Total distance = 80 + 80 = 160km

Average speed = (160/100)*39 = 62.4

questions.question: A bus driver must complete a 240 km trip in 4 hours. If he averages 70 km an hour for the first 3 hours of his trip. how fast must he travel (in km/h) in the last/final hour?
questions.questionHtml: A bus driver must complete a 240 km trip in 4 hours. If he averages 70 km an hour for the first 3 hours of his trip. how fast must he travel (in km/h) in the last/final hour?
questions.solution:
Distance covered in first 3 hours: Distance = 70 km/h × 3 hours = 210 km

Remaining distance: Total distance - Distance covered = 30 km

Speed = Distance / Time ⇒ 30 km / 1 hour = 30 km/h

questions.question: A police travelling at 65 km/h is chasing a thief who is 1200 m away from him and is travelling at 41 km/h. Find the time taken by the policeman to catch the thief.
questions.questionHtml: A police travelling at 65 km/h is chasing a thief who is 1200 m away from him and is travelling at 41 km/h. Find the time taken by the policeman to catch the thief.
questions.solution:
Given:

Speed of the policeman = 65 km/h

Speed of the thief = 41 km/h

Distance between the policeman and the thief = 1200 m

Formula Used:

Time = Distance / Relative Speed

Calculation:

Relative speed = Speed of the policeman - Speed of the thief

Relative speed = 65 - 41

Relative speed = 24 km/h

Convert 1200 m to km:

1200 m = 1200 / 1000 km = 1.2 km

Time taken to catch the thief = Distance / Relative Speed

⇒ Time taken to catch the thief = 1.2 km / 24 km/h

⇒ Time taken to catch the thief = 1.2 / 24

⇒ Time taken to catch the thief = 0.05 hours

Convert hours to minutes:

0.05 hours × 60 minutes/hour = 3 minutes

The time taken by the policeman to catch the thief is 3 minutes.

questions.question: A person covers 28 km while walking at a speed of 8 km/h. How much distance (in km) will he cover in same time if he walks at a speed of 6 km/h?
questions.questionHtml: A person covers 28 km while walking at a speed of 8 km/h. How much distance (in km) will he cover in same time if he walks at a speed of 6 km/h?
questions.solution:
The time taken to cover 28 km at 8 km/h

Time = 28 km / 8 km/h = 3.5 hours

New speed = 6 km/h

Distance = 6 km/h × 3.5 hours = 21 km

questions.question: A and B are at a distance of 1.7 km apart and they start running towards each other at a speed of 8 m/s and 9 m/s respectively. After how much time will take meet each other?
questions.questionHtml: A and B are at a distance of 1.7 km apart and they start running towards each other at a speed of 8 m/s and 9 m/s respectively. After how much time will take meet each other?
questions.solution:
Speed of A = 8 m/s and speed of B = 9 m/s

Distance between them = 1.7 km = 1700 m

If they running toward each other then speed = 8 + 9 = 17 m/s

As we know,

Time = Distance/speed

Time = 1700/17 = 100 second

As we know, 1 min = 60 sec

100 sec = 1 min 40 sec

questions.question: Ravi drove for 4 hours at a speed of 70 miles per hour and for 2 hours at 40 miles per hour. What was his average speed (in miles per hour) for the whole journey?
questions.questionHtml: Ravi drove for 4 hours at a speed of 70 miles per hour and for 2 hours at 40 miles per hour. What was his average speed (in miles per hour) for the whole journey?
questions.solution:
Distance covered in first 4 hours = 70 × 4 = 280 miles, Distance covered in next 2 hours = 40 × 2 = 80 miles

Total distance covered = 280 + 80 = 360 miles

Total time taken in the journey = 4 + 2 = 6 hours

Average speed = \(\frac{360}{6}\)= 60 miles/h.

questions.question: Two athletes are participating in a race on a circular track of 220 m. Ravi runs at the speed of 22 m/s, while Kapil runs at the speed of 11 m/s. They start from the same point, at the same time and in the same direction. After how many seconds will they meet for the first time?
questions.questionHtml: Two athletes are participating in a race on a circular track of 220 m. Ravi runs at the speed of 22 m/s, while Kapil runs at the speed of 11 m/s. They start from the same point, at the same time and in the same direction. After how many seconds will they meet for the first time?
questions.solution:
Relative speed = 22 m/s - 11 m/s = 11 m/s

⇒ Time = 220 m / 11 m/s = 20 seconds

questions.question: A car covers a distance of 90 km in 50 min. What is its speed (in m/s)?
questions.questionHtml: A car covers a distance of 90 km in 50 min. What is its speed (in m/s)?
questions.solution:
Given:

Distance = 90 km = 90,000 m

Time = 50 min = 50 × 60 = 3,000 s

Speed = Distance ÷ Time

⇒ Speed = 90,000 ÷ 3,000 = 30 m/s.

questions.question: A policeman sees a chain snatcher at a distance of 500 m. He starts chasing the chain snatcher who is running with a speed of 5 m/s while the policeman is chasing him with a speed of 15 m/s. What is the distance covered by the chain snatcher when he is caught by the policeman?
questions.questionHtml: A policeman sees a chain snatcher at a distance of 500 m. He starts chasing the chain snatcher who is running with a speed of 5 m/s while the policeman is chasing him with a speed of 15 m/s. What is the distance covered by the chain snatcher when he is caught by the policeman?
questions.solution:
Time taken to catch the snatcher 500 ÷ (15 - 5) = 50 seconds

Now, the distance covered by the chain snatcher when he is caught by the policeman = 50 × 5 = 250 m

questions.question: A dog saw a cat at a distance of 280 m. The cat started running at the speed of 10 km/h and the dog also ran to catch it with the speed of 24 km/h. How much time will the dog take to catch the cat?
questions.questionHtml: A dog saw a cat at a distance of 280 m. The cat started running at the speed of 10 km/h and the dog also ran to catch it with the speed of 24 km/h. How much time will the dog take to catch the cat?
questions.solution:
10 km/h = 25/9 m/s, 24 km/h = 20/3 m/s

⇒ 280 ÷ (20/3 - 25/9) ⇒ 72 seconds ⇒ 72/60 = 1.2 min

questions.question: The speed of a train is \(2\frac{1}{6}\) times the speed of a car. The car covers 486 km in 9 hours. How much distance will the train cover in 6 hours?
questions.questionHtml: The speed of a train is \(2\frac{1}{6}\) times the speed of a car. The car covers 486 km in 9 hours. How much distance will the train cover in 6 hours?
questions.solution:
Distance = 486 and time = 9 hours

Speed of the car = 486/9 = 54 km/hr

Speed of the train = 54 × (13/6) = 117 km/hr

Distance covered by train in 6 hrs = 117 × 6 = 702 km

questions.question: Ali and Badal start from the same position and at the same time in a 1200 m circular race, with speeds of 27 km/h and 45 km/h, respectively. Find after how much time they will meet again on the track for the first time when they are both running in the same direction.
questions.questionHtml: Ali and Badal start from the same position and at the same time in a 1200 m circular race, with speeds of 27 km/h and 45 km/h, respectively. Find after how much time they will meet again on the track for the first time when they are both running in the same direction.
questions.solution:
Relative speed of both in same direction = S2-S1=45 - 27 =18 km/h = 18 × (5/18) = 5 m/s.

Required Time = Length of track / relative speed in same direction = 1200/5 = 240 seconds

questions.question: A thief pursued by a policeman was 150 m ahead at the start. If the ratio of the speed of the policeman to that of the thief was 5 : 4, then how far (distance in metres) could the thief go before he is caught by the policeman?
questions.questionHtml: A thief pursued by a policeman was 150 m ahead at the start. If the ratio of the speed of the policeman to that of the thief was 5 : 4, then how far (distance in metres) could the thief go before he is caught by the policeman?
questions.solution:
Let speed of thief be 4x m/s

and speed of policeman be 5x m/s

Relative speed = x m/s

Time = 150 / x sec

Distance = 4x × 150 / x = 600 meters.

questions.question: A thief is spotted by a policeman from a distance of 195 metres. When the policeman starts the chase, the thief also starts running. If the speed of the thief is 22 km/h and that of the policeman is 27 km/h, then how far would the thief have run (in m) before he is overtaken?
questions.questionHtml: A thief is spotted by a policeman from a distance of 195 metres. When the policeman starts the chase, the thief also starts running. If the speed of the thief is 22 km/h and that of the policeman is 27 km/h, then how far would the thief have run (in m) before he is overtaken?
questions.solution:
Relative speed = Speedpoliceman - Speedthief = 7.5 m/s - 6.11 m/s = 1.39 m/s

Time = Distance / Relative speed = 195 m / 1.39 m/s ≈ 140.29 s

Distancethief = Speedthief × Time = 6.11 m/s × 140.29 s ≈ 856.77 m ≈ 858 m

questions.question: Two cities A and B are 135 km apart on a straight track. One car starts from A at 8 a.m. and travels towards B at 25 km/h. Another car starts from B at 9 a.m. and travels towards A at a speed of 30 km/h. At what time will they meet?
questions.questionHtml: Two cities A and B are 135 km apart on a straight track. One car starts from A at 8 a.m. and travels towards B at 25 km/h. Another car starts from B at 9 a.m. and travels towards A at a speed of 30 km/h. At what time will they meet?
questions.solution:
Let's assume that they meet after x hours after 8 a.m.

25x + 30(x-1) = 135 ⇒ 55x = 165 ⇒ x = 165/55 = 3 hr

The two cars will meet after 3 hours, so (8 a.m. + 3 hours) = 11 a.m.

questions.question: A policeman spotted a thief 40 metres ahead of him. The moment they both saw each other they started running in the same direction on the same track. The thief was running at 10 m/sec and the policeman was chasing him at the speed of 12 m/sec. How much distance (in metres) the policeman needed to cover to catch the thief?
questions.questionHtml: A policeman spotted a thief 40 metres ahead of him. The moment they both saw each other they started running in the same direction on the same track. The thief was running at 10 m/sec and the policeman was chasing him at the speed of 12 m/sec. How much distance (in metres) the policeman needed to cover to catch the thief?
questions.solution:
The relative speed of police and thief = 12 - 10 ⇒ 2 m/sec

Now, the total time is taken to catch the thief = 40/2 ⇒ 20 sec

So, distance traveled by the police = 20 × 12 ⇒ 240 m

questions.question: A train starts running at a uniform speed of 60 km/h from station P towards station Q. At the same time another train starts running from station Q towards station P. If the distance between the stations P and Q is 275 km and the trains meet in two and a half hours, then what is the speed of the train running towards station P in km/h?
questions.questionHtml: A train starts running at a uniform speed of 60 km/h from station P towards station Q. At the same time another train starts running from station Q towards station P. If the distance between the stations P and Q is 275 km and the trains meet in two and a half hours, then what is the speed of the train running towards station P in km/h?
questions.solution:
Alternate Method

Let the speed of both train be P and Q.

Meeting time = Distance/(P + Q)

⇒ 2.5 = 275/(60 + Q)

⇒ 150 + 2.5Q = 275

⇒ 2.5Q = 125

⇒ Q = 50 km/h

∴ The speed of Q is 50 km/h.

Traditional method:

Given:

Distance between P and Q = 275km

Calculation:

Let speed of train running towards station P be a kmph.

Relative speed = a + 60

Then,

⇒ a + 60 = 275/2.5

⇒ a + 60 = 110

⇒ a = 50

∴ speed of train running towards station P is 50 kmph.

questions.question: A thief is spotted by a policeman from a distance of 100 m. The thief starts running and the policeman chases him. If the speed of thief and policeman are 21 km/h and 23 km/h, respectively, then how far will the thief have to run before he is over taken?
questions.questionHtml: A thief is spotted by a policeman from a distance of 100 m. The thief starts running and the policeman chases him. If the speed of thief and policeman are 21 km/h and 23 km/h, respectively, then how far will the thief have to run before he is over taken?
questions.solution:
Relative Speed = 23 km/h - 21 km/h = 2 km/h

Convert 2 km/h to m/s: 2 × (5/18) = 5/9 m/s

Time = 100 m / (5/9 m/s) = 180 s

Speed of thief = 21 × (5/18) = 35/6 m/s

Distance = (35/6 m/s) × 180 s = 1050 m

questions.question: A vehicle is going at one-fourth of its usual speed and it takes an extra 45 minutes to reach its destination. Its usual time to cover the same distance is:
questions.questionHtml: A vehicle is going at one-fourth of its usual speed and it takes an extra 45 minutes to reach its destination. Its usual time to cover the same distance is:
questions.solution:
Let usual time = T hours

New time = 4T

Extra time taken = New time - usual time

⇒ 0.75 = 4T - T ⇒ 3T = 0.75 ⇒ T = 0.75/3 ⇒ T = 0.25 hours

questions.question: A thief is spotted by a policeman from a distance of 200 metres. When the policeman starts the chase, the thief also starts running. If the speed of the thief is 9 km/h and that of the policeman 10 km/h, how far will the thief have to run before he is overtaken?
questions.questionHtml: A thief is spotted by a policeman from a distance of 200 metres. When the policeman starts the chase, the thief also starts running. If the speed of the thief is 9 km/h and that of the policeman 10 km/h, how far will the thief have to run before he is overtaken?
questions.solution:
Relative speed = 10 km/h - 9 km/h = 1 km/h

Distance between thief and policeman = 200 meters = 0.2 km

Time to catch thief = 0.2 km / 1 km/h = 0.2 hours

Distance run by thief = 9 km/h × 0.2 hours = 1.8 km

questions.question: A and B are running on a circular track of length 1400 metres. The speed of A is 33 m/sec and the speed of B is 47 m/sec. They start from the same point at the same time in the opposite direction. After how much time will they meet for the second time?
questions.questionHtml: A and B are running on a circular track of length 1400 metres. The speed of A is 33 m/sec and the speed of B is 47 m/sec. They start from the same point at the same time in the opposite direction. After how much time will they meet for the second time?
questions.solution: Required time taken to meet for the second time =  2 × 1400 ÷ (33 + 47) = 2800 ÷ 80 = 35 sec

questions.question: A starts from a point at a speed of 34 m/s. After 5 seconds, B starts chasing A from the same point at a speed of 44 m/s. What will be the distance travelled by B before A is caught by B?
questions.questionHtml: A starts from a point at a speed of 34 m/s. After 5 seconds, B starts chasing A from the same point at a speed of 44 m/s. What will be the distance travelled by B before A is caught by B?
questions.solution:
Distance covered by A in 5 seconds = 34 × 5 = 170 m

Relative Speed of B w.r.t. A = (44 - 34) m/s = 10 m/s

Time taken by B to catch A = 170 / 10 = 17 seconds

Total distance covered by B = 17 × 44 = 748 m

questions.question: A thief is chased by a policeman and distance between them is 3 km. The speed of policeman is 75 km/h and the speed of the thief is 60 km/h. The policeman will be able to catch the thief when the thief would have covered the distance of ____________ km.
questions.questionHtml: A thief is chased by a policeman and distance between them is 3 km. The speed of policeman is 75 km/h and the speed of the thief is 60 km/h. The policeman will be able to catch the thief when the thief would have covered the distance of ____________ km.
questions.solution:
The relative speed between police and thief = (75 - 60) = 15 km/hr

⇒ Time taken = 3/15 = 1/5 = 1/5 × 60 min = 12 minutes

Distance travelled by a thief in 12 minutes = 60/60 × 12 = 12 km

questions.question: A policeman follows a thief who is 600 m ahead of the policeman. If the policeman and the thief run at speeds of 10 km/h and 8 km/h, respectively, in how much time (in minutes), will the policeman catch the thief?
questions.questionHtml: A policeman follows a thief who is 600 m ahead of the policeman. If the policeman and the thief run at speeds of 10 km/h and 8 km/h, respectively, in how much time (in minutes), will the policeman catch the thief?

questions.question: A policeman noticed a thief at some distance. The policeman started running to catch the thief and the thief also started running at the same time. The speed of both policeman and the thief was 12 km per hour and 10 km per hour, respectively. It took 30 minutes for the policeman to catch the thief. Find the initial distance (in metres) between them.
questions.questionHtml: A policeman noticed a thief at some distance. The policeman started running to catch the thief and the thief also started running at the same time. The speed of both policeman and the thief was 12 km per hour and 10 km per hour, respectively. It took 30 minutes for the policeman to catch the thief. Find the initial distance (in metres) between them.
questions.solution:
Relative Speed = 12 - 10 = 2 km/hour

Initial Distance = 2 km/hour × 0.5 hours = 1 km

Initial Distance = 1 km × 1000 = 1000 metres

questions.question: A thief stole jewellery from a shop at 8:15 p.m. and left on a bike at a speed of 60 km/h. The police were informed at 8:30 p.m. If the police want to arrest the thief at 9:00 p.m., what should be the minimum speed of the police jeep?
questions.questionHtml: A thief stole jewellery from a shop at 8:15 p.m. and left on a bike at a speed of 60 km/h. The police were informed at 8:30 p.m. If the police want to arrest the thief at 9:00 p.m., what should be the minimum speed of the police jeep?
questions.solution:
If the thief left at 8:15 p.m. and the police wants to catch him at 9:00 p.m., the time for which the thief was on the bike = 45 minutes = \(3 \over 4\) hours = 0.75 hours

Distance travelled by the thief = 60 km/h × 0.75 h = 45 km 

Time taken by the police to reach the thief = 30 minutes = 0.5 hours

Thus, minimum speed of the police jeep should be = \(45\: \text{km} \over 0.5 \:\text{h}\) = (45 × 2) km/h = 90 km/h

questions.question: In a circular race of 840 m, A and B start running in the same direction at the same time from the same point at the speeds of 6 m/s and 12 m/s, respectively. After how much time will they meet next?
questions.questionHtml: In a circular race of 840 m, A and B start running in the same direction at the same time from the same point at the speeds of 6 m/s and 12 m/s, respectively. After how much time will they meet next?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Since A and B are moving in the same direction, their relative speed is the difference between their speeds.

Relative Speed = 12 − 6 = 6 m/s

Time to meet next = Total Distance ÷ Relative Speed

Time = 840 ÷ 6 = 140 s

∴ The correct answer is 140 s.

Alternate Method

Given:

⇒ Length of circular track (D) = 840 m

⇒ Speed of A (SA) = 6 m/s

⇒ Speed of B (SB) = 12 m/s

Formula Used:

⇒ Relative Speed (same direction) = |SB − SA|

⇒ Time to meet = Total Distance ÷ Relative Speed

Calculations:

⇒ Relative Speed = 12 m/s − 6 m/s = 6 m/s

⇒ Time to meet = 840 ÷ 6

⇒ Time to meet = 140 s

∴ The correct answer is 140 s.

Additional Information

First Meeting Anywhere on Track

When two persons run in the same direction, they meet for the first time when the faster person covers exactly one more round than the slower person. Time = Length of Track ÷ Relative Speed.

First Meeting at Starting Point

The time taken to meet for the first time at the starting point is the LCM of the individual times taken by each person to complete one full round. Time = LCM(T1, T2).

Running in Opposite Directions

If two runners move in opposite directions, their relative speed is the sum of their individual speeds (S1 + S2). The time for their first meeting anywhere on the track is Track Length ÷ (S1 + S2).
